Maya Li: Heads up — I need to step out for a doctor's appointment at 14:05 PST. I'm going to hand primary to Jon for the 14:00-16:00 deploy window. I'm reachable by DM but reduced attention.
Jon Park: Ok picked up. Are there any active pages or ongoing incidents I should know about?
Maya Li: Nothing critical right now. We had a P1-like spike earlier but it's stable. Active items: low-latency alert in eu-west that's been flapping since 13:30, on monitor only. No current customer pages.
Kai Nguyen: I can take secondary for the window if Jon wants. I'll be on call at home but can jump into Zoom if needed.
Jon Park: Thanks Kai — please standby as secondary. Maya, can you paste the quick runbook steps and any knobs I should try first if latency spikes?
Maya Li: Yep — runbook gist: quick checklist
```
1) Check /dash/latency & tail nginx errors for 5m: `kubectl logs -l app=proxy -n prod --since=5m`
2) If 502s rising, toggle canary fallback: `curl -XPOST https://ops/api/fallback?canary=false`
3) If CPU on inference nodes >85% scale group +1 via autoscaler: `infractl scale set --pool llm-prod --replicas +1`
4) If it's a model OOM, swap to quantized variant: set model.param "variant=lite" in Redwood Console
```
Also the deploy's preflight job should run at 14:10 — be ready to abort if preflight fails.
ops-runbook-bot: Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/latency-eu-west (last updated 2026-02-28)
pagerbot: On-call reassignment in progress: re-routing primary pages to @Jon Park for 14:00 - 16:00 PST...
pagerbot: Done — pager routing updated. Test page sent to Jon.
incident-bot: NOTE: Low-severity latency alert from eu-west-1 at 13:50 UTC — monitoring only.
Jon Park: Got the test page, audible. Thanks. I'll monitor/handle any incoming pages. Kai, please take pager escalation if something needs SRE escalation.
Kai Nguyen: Affirmative — will escalate to SRE if I see infra issues.
Santiago R.: Quick Q: any customer-impacting jobs running during the window (batch jobs, nightly evals)? We should avoid running those if possible.
Maya Li: Verified: nightly-evals scheduled at 23:00 UTC, no batch load during window. The only user-facing change is a canary deploy to the embed-service at 14:15.
Jon Park: For the canary — if latency moves >20% on the canary metric within 5m, I'll abort and roll back. Maya: what's the rollback command?
Maya Li: `deployctl rollback embed-service --to-tag stable && deployctl notify '#infra-ops' "embed-service rollback"`
Jon Park: Copy. I'll add a quick dashboard watch and set a 5m alert rule for the canary metric at +20%.
Maya Li: Thanks. One more: if you need a fast mitigation for model-cost-induced latency, we can temporarily reduce batch_size on the runner: `rdwctl set-config runner.batch_size=8` — reduces throughput but lowers tail latency.
Jon Park: Noted.
Kai Nguyen: If anything fires and I need to escalate to SRE, call me on phone; I'll ping #eng-sre as well.
Maya Li: Leaving the thread — thanks all. Jon/Kai, appreciate the cover.
Jon Park: Taking over primary now. I'll post update at end of window or earlier if anything happens. :thumbsup:
